section_1.title: From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition
section_1.content: Briefly review 2D/3D vectors as arrows. Introduce the shift: what if 'vectors' aren't just arrows, but functions or polynomials? Define a vector space as a collection of objects that satisfy specific rules (Closure, Additivity, Scaling).
section_1.example: Visualize a 2D arrow turning into a musical wave function. Both are 'vectors' because they can be scaled (volume/length) and added (combining sounds/positions).

section_2.title: The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms
section_2.content: Present the 8 formal axioms (associativity, commutativity, zero vector, inverse, etc.) as the 'rules of the game.' Use a visual table where checks mark compliance for both traditional arrows and abstract objects.
section_2.example: Use 'Space-Bot,' a robot character that can only perform operations that follow these 8 rules. If an operation breaks the rules, Space-Bot errors out.

section_3.title: Example: The Polynomial Vector Space
section_3.content: Demonstrate that the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 is a vector space. Show addition (p(x) + q(x)) and scalar multiplication (c * p(x)) graphically by shifting and stretching curves.
section_3.example: Represent a quadratic polynomial as a set of 'DNA markers' (coefficients a, b, c). Show how adding two polynomials is just adding their DNA markers, proving they behave like standard vectors.

section_4.title: Application: The Geometry of Data
section_4.content: Connect abstract spaces to real-world applications. Explain that machine learning represents images or documents as vectors in high-dimensional 'feature spaces.'
section_4.example: Imagine a 'Mood-Space' where different emojis are vectors. The sum of a 'Happy' vector and a 'Party' vector creates a new 'Ecstatic' vector in the same abstract space.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap: Abstract vector spaces are not about 'shapes,' but about 'logical structure.' Emphasize that stripping away physical form allows us to solve complex problems in physics, economics, and AI.
section_5.example: Final visual: A collection of diverse items (arrows, waves, lists, polynomials) merging into a single 'Library of Vectors,' signifying the unifying power of linear algebra.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition", ["Vectors are more than just arrows.", "Think of waves or polynomials.", "Objects sharing common logical rules."])
        
        # Define objects
        circles = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(3)])
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.1, color="#00CED1") for _ in range(3)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        for i, circle in enumerate(circles):
            self.place_at_grid(circle, f"B{2+i}")
        self.play(FadeIn(circles))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        
        # Morphing
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(circles, dots))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["C5"], color="#FFFFFF")
        self.add(arrow)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Polynomials form a vector space.", "Adding polynomials adds their DNA.", "Scaling stretches the polynomial curve."]
        self.setup_layout("Example: The Polynomial Vector Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a polynomial p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c (#FF4500)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.6)
        p_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5*x**2 + x + 1, color="#FF4500")
        p_label = MathTex("p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c", color="#FF4500").scale(0.7)
        
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, p_curve), "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(p_curve), Write(p_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Break coefficients into distinct basis component vectors (#32CD32)
        dna_markers = VGroup(
            Vector([0, 1, 0], color="#32CD32"),
            Vector([1, 0, 0], color="#32CD32"),
            Vector([0, 0, 1], color="#32CD32")

        self.place_at_grid(axes3d, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(vectors, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(axes3d), Create(vectors))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of Data", [
            "Data lives in feature spaces.",
            "Emojis act as coordinate vectors.",
            "Adding moods creates new feelings."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a cloud of data points (#8A2BE2)
        data_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#8A2BE2") for _ in range(20)])
        for p in data_points:
            p.move_to(np.array([
                np.random.uniform(1.5, 6.5),
                np.random.uniform(-1.5, 2.0),
                0
            ]))
        self.play(FadeIn(data_points))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#8A2BE2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a line of best fit emerging through the cloud (#FFFFFF)
        line = Line(start=np.array([1.5, -0.5, 0]), end=np.array([6.5, 1.5, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the orthogonal projection lines from points to the fit
        projections = VGroup()
        for p in data_points:
            # Simple projection point on line
            t = np.dot(p.get_center() - line.get_start(), line.get_vector()) / np.dot(line.get_vector(), line.get_vector())
            proj = line.get_start() + np.clip(t, 0, 1) * line.get_vector()
            projections.add(Line(p.get_center(), proj, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2))
        
        self.play(Create(projections))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition
section_1.content: Briefly review 2D/3D vectors as arrows. Introduce the shift: what if 'vectors' aren't just arrows, but functions or polynomials? Define a vector space as a collection of objects that satisfy specific rules (Closure, Additivity, Scaling).
section_1.example: Visualize a 2D arrow turning into a musical wave function. Both are 'vectors' because they can be scaled (volume/length) and added (combining sounds/positions).

section_2.title: The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms
section_2.content: Present the 8 formal axioms (associativity, commutativity, zero vector, inverse, etc.) as the 'rules of the game.' Use a visual table where checks mark compliance for both traditional arrows and abstract objects.
section_2.example: Use 'Space-Bot,' a robot character that can only perform operations that follow these 8 rules. If an operation breaks the rules, Space-Bot errors out.

section_3.title: Example: The Polynomial Vector Space
section_3.content: Demonstrate that the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 is a vector space. Show addition (p(x) + q(x)) and scalar multiplication (c * p(x)) graphically by shifting and stretching curves.
section_3.example: Represent a quadratic polynomial as a set of 'DNA markers' (coefficients a, b, c). Show how adding two polynomials is just adding their DNA markers, proving they behave like standard vectors.

section_4.title: Application: The Geometry of Data
section_4.content: Connect abstract spaces to real-world applications. Explain that machine learning represents images or documents as vectors in high-dimensional 'feature spaces.'
section_4.example: Imagine a 'Mood-Space' where different emojis are vectors. The sum of a 'Happy' vector and a 'Party' vector creates a new 'Ecstatic' vector in the same abstract space.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap: Abstract vector spaces are not about 'shapes,' but about 'logical structure.' Emphasize that stripping away physical form allows us to solve complex problems in physics, economics, and AI.
section_5.example: Final visual: A collection of diverse items (arrows, waves, lists, polynomials) merging into a single 'Library of Vectors,' signifying the unifying power of linear algebra.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition", ["Vectors are more than just arrows.", "Think of waves or polynomials.", "Objects sharing common logical rules."])
        
        # Define objects
        circles = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(3)])
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.1, color="#00CED1") for _ in range(3)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        for i, circle in enumerate(circles):
            self.place_at_grid(circle, f"B{2+i}")
        self.play(FadeIn(circles))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        
        # Morphing
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(circles, dots))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["C5"], color="#FFFFFF")
        self.add(arrow)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms", ["Eight axioms define the game.", "Space-Bot strictly obeys these rules.", "Violations trigger a logical error."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_C)
        axiom_cards = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.8, width=1.2, color="#4682B4", fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(8)])
        for i, card in enumerate(axiom_cards):
            card.add(Text(f"A{i+1}", font_size=20))
            # Use valid grid keys: i//4 maps to 0 or 1 (row A or B), i%4 maps to 0-3 (col 1-4)
            self.place_at_grid(card, f"{'AB'[i//4]}{i%4 + 1}")
        
        self.play(Create(axiom_cards))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN_C)
        
        for card in axiom_cards:
            self.play(card.animate.set_color(GREEN_B), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Create central stack
        stack = VGroup(*axiom_cards).copy().arrange(UP, buff=-0.6)
        stack_title = Text("The 8 Rules", font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(stack, stack_title).arrange(DOWN), "C3", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(axiom_cards, stack), Write(stack_title))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED_C)
        
        error_sign = Text("ERROR!", font_size=40, color=RED, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(error_sign, "D6")
        self.play(FadeIn(error_sign, scale=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(stack))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of Data", [
            "Data lives in feature spaces.",
            "Emojis act as coordinate vectors.",
            "Adding moods creates new feelings."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a cloud of data points (#8A2BE2)
        data_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#8A2BE2") for _ in range(20)])
        for p in data_points:
            p.move_to(np.array([
                np.random.uniform(1.5, 6.5),
                np.random.uniform(-1.5, 2.0),
                0
            ]))
        self.play(FadeIn(data_points))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#8A2BE2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a line of best fit emerging through the cloud (#FFFFFF)
        line = Line(start=np.array([1.5, -0.5, 0]), end=np.array([6.5, 1.5, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the orthogonal projection lines from points to the fit
        projections = VGroup()
        for p in data_points:
            # Simple projection point on line
            t = np.dot(p.get_center() - line.get_start(), line.get_vector()) / np.dot(line.get_vector(), line.get_vector())
            proj = line.get_start() + np.clip(t, 0, 1) * line.get_vector()
            projections.add(Line(p.get_center(), proj, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2))
        
        self.play(Create(projections))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

        for p in data_points:

            line_vec = line.get_vector()

        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        emoji = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/emoji.svg")

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms", ["Eight axioms define the game.", "Space-Bot strictly obeys these rules.", "Violations trigger a logical error."])
        
        asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/card.png"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#4682B4")
        
        axiom_cards = Group()

        for card in axiom_cards:

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
